author: Albert Hofmann Sandoz Archive & Athanor Ascension ChemLab
description: Complete chemical suite of Albert Hofmann's historic Sandoz Basel laboratory research (1938–1971): Ergot alkaloid isolation, alkaline hydrolysis to D-lysergic acid, LSD-25 semisynthesis and diastereomer isomerization, Methergine, Hydergine, ALD-52, 1P-LSD, LSA/Ergine, and Psilocybin/Psilocin isolation and total chemical synthesis.

protocols.name: Ergot Alkaloid Extraction (Claviceps purpurea)
protocols.description: Extraction and isolation of ergotamine and ergometrine from Claviceps purpurea rye sclerotia (Mutterkorn) using tartaric acid extraction, basification with ammonia, and chloroform liquid-liquid partition (Albert Hofmann, Sandoz Basel, 1930s).

catalyst.name: Ammonium hydroxide (conc. NH4OH to pH 9.2)
catalyst.description: Basifying agent to liberate free-base ergot peptide alkaloids

sop_steps: Defat pulverized ergot rye sclerotia with petroleum ether in a Soxhlet extractor.
Macerate defatted cake with 2% aqueous tartaric acid solution at 30 °C under dim yellow light (protect from UV photodecomposition).
Filter marc under vacuum through Buchner funnel.
Cool acidic aqueous extract in ice bath and basify carefully with concentrated NH4OH to pH 9.2.
Extract aqueous suspension 4x with equal volumes of chloroform.
Combine chloroform extracts, dry over anhydrous sodium sulfate (Na2SO4), and evaporate under reduced pressure on rotovap.
Recrystallize crude ergotamine tartrate from aqueous acetone.

protocols.name: D-Lysergic Acid (Alkaline Ergotamine Cleavage)
protocols.description: Alkaline saponification of ergotamine or ergonovine with aqueous methanolic potassium hydroxide to hydrolyze the peptide moiety, followed by isoelectric precipitation of pure D-lysergic acid at pH 5.5 (Albert Hofmann, 1938).

catalyst.name: Nitrogen atmosphere purge
catalyst.description: Inert gas blanket to prevent atmospheric oxidation to lumilysergic acids

sop_steps: Charge 20.0 g ergotamine tartrate into a 250 mL round-bottom flask equipped with reflux condenser and nitrogen inlet.
Add 120 mL of 4M methanolic potassium hydroxide solution.
Heat mixture to reflux (75 °C) under dry nitrogen purge in darkness for 75 minutes.
Cool reaction flask in ice bath to 10 °C and dilute with 80 mL cold degassed water.
Adjust pH carefully to 5.5 (isoelectric point of lysergic acid) using cold concentrated hydrochloric acid.
D-lysergic acid precipitates immediately as fine gray-white hexagonal microcrystals.
Collect crystals by vacuum filtration on sintered glass funnel, wash with cold water and diethyl ether, and dry in vacuum desiccator.

protocols.name: LSD-25 (D-Lysergic Acid Diethylamide)
protocols.description: Semisynthetic peptide coupling of anhydrous D-lysergic acid with diethylamine via trifluoroacetic anhydride (TFAA) mixed anhydride activation under amber safety lighting and nitrogen atmosphere (Albert Hofmann, Sandoz Basel, November 1938; resynthesized April 16/19, 1943).

catalyst.name: Trifluoroacetic anhydride (TFAA in acetonitrile)
catalyst.description: Mixed anhydride activating agent forming lysergic-trifluoroacetic mixed anhydride

sop_steps: Suspend 10.73 g (40 mmol) finely ground anhydrous D-lysergic acid in 100 mL dry acetonitrile at -15 °C under argon.
Add dropwise 10.5 mL (75 mmol) trifluoroacetic anhydride over 15 minutes with vigorous magnetic stirring. The acid dissolves completely as amber mixed anhydride.
Stir at -10 °C for 30 minutes, then warm to 0 °C.
Add dropwise a solution of 8.78 g (120 mmol) distilled anhydrous diethylamine in 40 mL acetonitrile over 20 minutes.
Allow reaction mixture to warm to room temperature (20 °C) and stir for 3 hours protected from light.
Pour into 250 mL ice-cold water, basify with 20% sodium hydroxide to pH 9.5, and extract 4x with 75 mL dichloromethane.
Wash organic extracts with saturated sodium chloride, dry over anhydrous Na2SO4, and evaporate solvent below 30 °C under vacuum.
Crude product contains ~65% D-LSD and ~35% D-iso-LSD.

protocols.name: D-LSD Tartrate & Iso-LSD Isomerization
protocols.description: Chromatographic separation of active D-LSD ([α]D = +17°) from inactive D-iso-LSD ([α]D = +281°) over neutral alumina, followed by basic isomerization of D-iso-LSD back to D-LSD with dilute methanolic KOH, and crystallization as D-LSD (+)-tartrate (Albert Hofmann, 1943).

catalyst.name: Methanolic potassium hydroxide (0.1M KOH)
catalyst.description: Base catalyst for C8 epimerization of D-iso-LSD to D-LSD

sop_steps: Dissolve crude diastereomeric mixture in 25 mL chloroform and load onto neutral alumina column (Brockmann grade I).
Elute with chloroform: D-iso-LSD elutes first (fluoresces intense blue under 366 nm UV).
Elute D-LSD with chloroform containing 0.5% methanol. Combine pure D-LSD fractions and concentrate under vacuum.
Take isolated D-iso-LSD fractions, dissolve in 50 mL 0.1M methanolic KOH, and heat at 40 °C under nitrogen for 45 minutes to re-equilibrate (yields 65:35 D-LSD:D-iso-LSD).
Evaporate, wash, and re-chromatograph to recover recycled D-LSD.
Dissolve pure D-LSD base in 20 mL warm absolute methanol and add stoichiometric L-(+)-tartaric acid (1 mole tartaric acid per 2 moles LSD).
Add dry diethyl ether until faint cloudiness forms, seed, and cool at -10 °C overnight.
Collect pure white needles of D-lysergic acid diethylamide (+)-tartrate, mp 198-200 °C (dec).

protocols.name: Methergine (Methylergonovine)
protocols.description: Albert Hofmann's celebrated synthetic uterotonic medicine developed at Sandoz Basel for obstetrics: coupling of D-lysergic acid azide or mixed anhydride with optically active (+)-2-aminobutanol (1940s).
sop_steps: Prepare D-lysergic acid chloride or mixed anhydride at -15 °C in dry THF under nitrogen.
Add 5.35 g (+)-2-amino-1-butanol and 5.5 mL triethylamine in dry THF dropwise over 20 minutes.
Stir at 20 °C for 2 hours protected from light.
Quench in cold water, extract with chloroform, and wash with dilute sodium carbonate.
Isolate methylergonovine free base and convert to maleate salt with maleic acid in absolute ethanol.
Recrystallize pure methylergonovine maleate (Methergine), essential medicine for postpartum hemorrhage control.

protocols.name: Hydergine (Ergoloid Mesylates Hydrogenation)
protocols.description: Catalytic hydrogenation of the 9,10-double bond of natural ergot peptide alkaloids (ergocristine, ergocornine, ergocryptine) over palladium on charcoal to eliminate peripheral vasoconstriction while preserving central metabolic activity (Albert Hofmann, Sandoz 1940s).

reagent_b.name: Hydrogen gas (H2, 2.5 atm in Parr shaker)

sop_steps: Dissolve 15.0 g natural ergotoxine base mixture in 120 mL ethanol containing 20 mL glacial acetic acid.
Add 1.5 g 10% Pd/C catalyst to a Parr hydrogenation pressure vessel under nitrogen purge.
Pressurize vessel with hydrogen gas to 2.5 atm and agitate at 40 °C until hydrogen uptake ceases (approx. 4 hours).
Filter catalyst carefully through Celite pad under nitrogen (pyrophoric!).
Concentrate filtrate, neutralize with aqueous ammonia, and extract with ethyl acetate.
Convert to mesylate salt with methanesulfonic acid in methanol to yield Hydergine (ergoloid mesylates).

protocols.name: ALD-52 (1-Acetyl-LSD)
protocols.description: Acetylation of the indole N1 position of D-lysergic acid diethylamide using acetic anhydride in anhydrous pyridine or trifluoroacetic anhydride catalyzed acetylation (Albert Hofmann & Franz Troxler, Sandoz, 1957).

catalyst.name: Anhydrous pyridine / DMAP
catalyst.description: Base catalyst for indole nitrogen nucleophilic acylation

sop_steps: Dissolve 3.23 g D-LSD free base in 15 mL anhydrous pyridine under argon.
Add 4.5 mL freshly distilled acetic anhydride and a catalytic crystal of 4-dimethylaminopyridine (DMAP).
Heat at 50 °C for 2 hours in darkness under inert atmosphere.
Evaporate excess pyridine and acetic anhydride under high vacuum below 40 °C.
Dissolve residue in dichloromethane, wash with cold 5% sodium bicarbonate solution and water.
Dry over Na2SO4, evaporate, and recrystallize ALD-52 from diethyl ether.

protocols.name: LSA / Ergine (Ipomoea tricolor Seed Isolation)
protocols.description: Extraction and isolation of D-lysergic acid amide (ergine) and isoergine from the sacred Mexican seeds Ololiuqui (Rivea corymbosa) and Badoh Negro (Ipomoea tricolor) via petroleum ether defatting and cold methanol extraction (Albert Hofmann, 1960).

catalyst.name: Tartaric acid (0.5% in methanol)
catalyst.description: Acid stabilizer preventing photo-oxidation of clavine alkaloids

sop_steps: Grind 100 g Ipomoea tricolor seeds to a fine meal in darkness.
Defat seed meal 3x with 150 mL petroleum ether to remove nausea-inducing glycosides and fatty oils.
Dry the defatted seed cake in vacuum desiccator.
Macerate defatted meal with 300 mL cold methanol containing 0.5% tartaric acid for 3 hours in darkness.
Filter and concentrate methanolic extract to 50 mL under vacuum at 25 °C.
Dilute with water, basify with ammonium hydroxide to pH 8.8, and extract 3x with chloroform.
Evaporate chloroform and crystallize pure Ergine (LSA) as colorless prisms.

protocols.name: Psilocybin Total Chemical Synthesis (Hofmann 1958)
protocols.description: Total chemical synthesis of 4-phosphoryloxy-N,N-dimethyltryptamine (psilocybin) from 4-benzyloxyindole via Speeter-Anthony oxalyl chloride acylation, LiAlH4 reduction to 4-benzyloxy-DMT, catalytic hydrogenolysis to psilocin, and phosphorylation with dibenzyl phosphorochloridate (Albert Hofmann, Sandoz Basel, 1958).

reagent_b.name: Oxalyl chloride in anhydrous diethyl ether

sop_steps: Dissolve 11.16 g (50 mmol) 4-benzyloxyindole in 150 mL anhydrous diethyl ether at 0 °C.
Add dropwise 7.0 g (55 mmol) oxalyl chloride in ether with stirring. Orange crystals of 4-benzyloxyindol-3-yl-glyoxylyl chloride separate.
Add excess cold anhydrous dimethylamine solution in ether. Filter the resulting glyoxylamide and wash with water.
Reduce the glyoxylamide with 8.0 g LiAlH4 in boiling dry THF for 4 hours to yield 4-benzyloxy-DMT.
Cleave the benzyl ether protecting group via catalytic hydrogenation over 10% Pd/C in methanol to yield pure crystalline Psilocin (4-HO-DMT, mp 173-176 °C).
Phosphorylate psilocin free base at -20 °C using dibenzyl phosphorochloridate in pyridine.
Remove benzyl phosphate esters by catalytic hydrogenolysis over Pd/C in methanol.
Recrystallize pure Psilocybin from boiling water/ethanol as white sparkling needles, mp 220-228 °C.

protocols.name: Psilocybin & Psilocin Mushroom Isolation
protocols.description: First chemical isolation and crystallization of pure psilocybin and psilocin from laboratory-cultivated mycelium and carpophores of Psilocybe mexicana Heim collected in Huautla de Jiménez, Oaxaca, Mexico (Albert Hofmann, Roger Heim, Arthur Brack, Hans Kobel, Sandoz Basel, 1958).
sop_steps: Macerate 50 g dried powdered Psilocybe mexicana carpophores 3x with 200 mL methanol at 40 °C for 90 minutes.
Filter extracts and concentrate under vacuum on rotovap below 35 °C to a dark syrup.
Dissolve syrup in water, defat with petroleum ether and diethyl ether.
Chromatograph aqueous solution over cellulose powder column eluted with water-saturated n-butanol.
Monitor fractions with Keller's reagent (iron(III) chloride in glacial acetic acid + sulfuric acid -> deep blue-violet).
Crystallize pure Psilocybin from boiling water as colorless fine needles.
Psilocin is obtained from subsequent butanol fractions as prismatic crystals from benzene.
